routes.description: Establish at least one first cause by excluding causal loops and infinite regress, apply the causal principle to make that cause beginningless and initially changeless, distinguish it from material reality, and infer personal agency from its capacity to originate the universe without prior determination.
routes.successCriteria: The pro burden is satisfied if the defended causal structure and causal principle require at least one beginningless, transcendent first cause, and if originating a first change from an initially changeless condition warrants attributing libertarian agency and personhood to that creator.

motionBridge.description: Connect a beginningless and initially changeless first cause to a personal creator capable of freely originating the universe.

centralBridges.description: Exclude both an infinite causal regress and a closed causal loop so that the causal series terminates in at least one first cause.
Defend the principle that whatever begins to exist has a cause against the proposed causeless initial natural state.
Show that the first cause lacks a beginning and is initially changeless because beginnings and changes fall within the causal principle.
Show that the first cause is nonmaterial and can originate an undetermined first event while retaining the capacity not to change.

subsidiaryBridges.description: Supply distinctions and supporting arguments concerning dynamic loops, static circular dependence, and infinite causal regress.
Clarify states, events, directional finitude, and the relevant modal status of a beginningless unsustained cause.

routes.description: Deny that the reformulated Kalam uniquely establishes its conclusion by challenging the exclusions and property inferences required for the creator route, presenting a necessary initial natural state as a rival foundation, and comparing the complete theories for consistency, explanatory coverage, and economy.
routes.successCriteria: The con burden is satisfied if a coherent necessary-initial-state theory accounts for the causal and explanatory data without a personal creator, or if the pro premises fail to establish a beginningless, changeless, transcendent personal cause rather than a universe-internal first state.

motionBridge.description: Establish that the relevant facts permit a universe-internal initial cause and do not require a beginningless personal creator outside the universe.

centralBridges.description: Show that the causal premises do not conclusively exclude regress or loops and at most yield one or more uncaused causes without the further creator properties.
Defend a metaphysically necessary initial natural state whose necessity explains its existence and whose causal evolution explains later reality.
Test whether beginninglessness and changelessness coherently apply to a timeless cause without reintroducing an extension, regress, or absolute beginning.
Compare the rival theories by explanatory reach, consistency, modal commitments, and ontological economy rather than presuming the disputed causal premises.

subsidiaryBridges.description: Clarify causal relata, causal-loop assumptions, event beginnings, and the distinction between initial and non-initial reality.
Distinguish logical consistency, metaphysical possibility, actual-world persistence, and ultimate unexplained necessity.

sections.title: First Causes, Infinite Regress, and Causal Loops
sections.rationale: This issue determines whether the causal series must terminate in at least one first cause and therefore supplies the indispensable starting point for either a creator inference or a universe-internal initial-cause account.

sections.title: The Causal Principle and a Necessary Initial Natural State
sections.rationale: The central clash is whether every beginning requires a cause or whether a metaphysically necessary initial natural state may begin causelessly while grounding the causal explanation of all later reality.

sections.title: Necessity, Possibility, and Ultimate Explanation
sections.rationale: The rival accounts depend on whether necessity can explain an initial state, whether beginninglessness supports necessity, and whether logically consistent alternatives count as metaphysically possible alternatives requiring selection.

sections.title: Beginninglessness, Timelessness, Events, and Change
sections.rationale: This issue governs whether the proposed first cause can coherently be timeless, beginningless, and initially changeless, and whether an initial event or state escapes or falls under the relevant causal principle.

sections.title: Personal Agency and Comparative Explanatory Burden
sections.rationale: The motion ultimately requires a bridge from a first cause to a personal creator, while the competing route asks whether libertarian agency adds explanatory value beyond a simpler universe-internal natural foundation.
